acceptance: A baseline date in the future fails the ratchet with a message that names the date
A lane diff that moves the date forward is refused
Lowering count in the same commit as a removed copy still passes
fix: Treat the date as gate configuration, not lane data: reject a date later than today in ParseBaseline or Check, and refuse a diff that moves the date forward; or move the date to a protected file and leave only count lane-writable. Fold into the content-keyed baseline design of testdup-equal-count-conflicts-across-lanes if that lands first.
source: console, 2026-11-10, adversarial review of the protection follow-up (incident 2026-11-09)
summary: go/.test-dup-baseline is unprotected so lanes can lower count. Its date field selects which acs/ directories testdup.Scan reads (isOld, go/internal/testdup/testdup.go). A lane that writes date=2099-01-01 makes every acs directory old: the TDD handoff floor finds no copy and the ship ratchet skips acs, and the equal-count rule lets the lane lower count in the same commit. Found by adversarial review of the protection follow-up (MEDIUM, residual).
title: The duplicate ratchet's baseline date is lane-writable and can switch off the acs scope
